# 2 Kings Chapter 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 232r–233r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_011_page_001.jpg, 2KI_011_page_002.jpg, 2KI_011_page_003.jpg

---

**1** When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, learned that her son was dead, she moved swiftly to destroy every member of the royal family.

**2** But Jehosheba — daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah — snatched the infant Joash from among the princes who were being slaughtered. She hid him and his nurse in a bedroom, keeping him out of Athaliah's reach. He survived.

**3** For six years, he remained hidden in the temple of the LORD while Athaliah ruled the land.

**4** In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest made his move. He summoned the commanders of the Carite mercenaries and the royal guard, brought them into the temple, made a covenant with them, swore them to secrecy — and then showed them the king's son.

**5** He gave them their orders: "Here is the plan. A third of you who come on duty on the Sabbath will guard the royal palace.

**6** A third will be stationed at the Sur Gate, and a third at the gate behind the guards. You will form a defensive perimeter around the palace.

**7** The two divisions going off duty on the Sabbath will guard the temple of the LORD, surrounding the king.

**8** Station yourselves around the king, weapons in hand. Anyone who breaks through the ranks — kill them. Stay with the king wherever he goes."

**9** The commanders carried out Jehoiada's plan exactly. Each one took his men — both those coming on duty and those going off — and reported to Jehoiada the priest.

**10** The priest distributed the spears and ceremonial shields that had belonged to King David, which had been stored in the temple.

**11** The guards took their positions, weapons drawn, lining both sides of the temple from south to north, flanking the altar and the building, forming a wall around the king.

**12** Then Jehoiada brought out the prince. He placed the crown on his head and presented him with the covenant document. They proclaimed him king and anointed him. The people clapped and shouted, "Long live the king!"

**13** Athaliah heard the commotion — the guards, the cheering people — and rushed to the temple.

**14** There she saw the new king standing by the pillar in the traditional place of coronation, surrounded by officers and trumpeters, with the whole country celebrating and blowing trumpets. She ripped her robes and screamed, "Treason! Treason!"

**15** Jehoiada the priest ordered the military commanders, "Take her out through the ranks. Kill with the sword anyone who tries to defend her." He added, "She must not be executed inside the LORD's temple."

**16** They seized her and dragged her through the horses' entrance to the palace, and there they killed her.

**17** Then Jehoiada established a covenant — between the LORD, the king, and the people — that they would be the LORD's people. He also made a covenant between the king and the people.

**18** The entire nation surged to the temple of Baal and demolished it. They smashed the altars and the idols to pieces and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, right in front of his own altars. Jehoiada then stationed guards at the LORD's temple.

**19** He assembled the commanders, the Carites, the royal guard, and all the people, and they escorted the king down from the temple, through the guards' gate, and into the palace. Joash took his seat on the royal throne.

**20** The whole country celebrated, and the city was at peace. As for Athaliah — she had been executed at the palace.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — Athaliah's massacre:** She is the only woman to rule either kingdom, and she seizes power through the most brutal means possible — murdering her own grandchildren. She is also the daughter (or granddaughter) of Ahab and Jezebel, extending the house of Omri's influence into Judah.

**Verse 4 — Jehoiada's coup:** The priest waits six years. This is not impulsive — it is a carefully planned military operation executed by a religious leader. The temple becomes both a sanctuary for the child and the staging ground for the revolution.

**Verse 12 — Crown and testimony:** The coronation involves two objects: a crown (political authority) and a testimony document (covenantal obligation). Israelite kingship is never absolute — it comes with a written contract between the king and God.

**Verse 17 — Double covenant:** Jehoiada is rebuilding society from the ground up. One covenant reconnects the nation to YHWH; the other establishes the proper relationship between ruler and ruled. After years of illegitimate, Baal-worshipping tyranny, both covenants are necessary.

**Verse 18 — The Baal temple destroyed:** The demolition of Baal worship in Jerusalem mirrors what Jehu did in the north (ch. 10). Athaliah had imported Baalism from her Omride heritage. Her death and the temple's destruction are a single act of purification.

*— PNEUMA*
